gitConfigDefaultBranchHint: Used by git init for new repositories (init.defaultBranch).
gitConfigAutocrlfHint: How Git converts LF/CRLF. Does not change Giter fetch or update.
gitConfigFetchPruneHint: Remove stale remote-tracking branches during git fetch.
gitConfigPullFfHint: How git pull behaves in the terminal. Giter Update always uses --ff-only.
gitConfigPushDefaultHint: Which branch git push updates when no refspec is given.
gitConfigColorUiHint: Colored Git output in the terminal.
gitConfigHelpDefaultBranchIntro: This is init.defaultBranch — the name git init gives the first branch in a new repository.
gitConfigHelpDefaultBranchEmpty: Leave it unset to keep Git’s own default (often master on older Git; some versions ask).
gitConfigHelpDefaultBranchMain: main is what GitHub and recent Git usually use.
gitConfigHelpDefaultBranchMaster: master is the old default. A few older tools still assume it.
gitConfigHelpAutocrlfIntro: Whether Git rewrites LF/CRLF when you commit or check out. Giter Fetch and Update ignore this.
gitConfigHelpAutocrlfUnset: Default keeps Git’s built-in behavior (usually Off on macOS/Linux; Windows setup often picks CRLF).
gitConfigHelpAutocrlfFalse: Off leaves files as stored. Use this when the repo is already LF-only.
gitConfigHelpAutocrlfInput: Input converts CRLF to LF on commit and does not convert on checkout. Typical on macOS and Linux.
gitConfigHelpAutocrlfTrue: CRLF checks out as CRLF and commits as LF. Typical on Windows.
gitConfigHelpFetchPruneIntro: Whether git fetch deletes local remote-tracking branches that no longer exist on the remote.
gitConfigHelpFetchPruneUnset: Default does not prune unless you pass --prune. Giter’s own Fetch already uses --prune.
gitConfigHelpFetchPruneOff: Off keeps stale origin/… branches after fetch.
gitConfigHelpFetchPruneOn: On removes those stale remote-tracking branches during fetch.
gitConfigHelpPullFfIntro: How git pull behaves in a terminal. Giter Update always uses --ff-only, regardless of this setting.
gitConfigHelpPullFfUnset: Default matches Yes on current Git: fast-forward when possible, otherwise merge.
gitConfigHelpPullFfTrue: Yes fast-forwards when it can; otherwise it creates a merge commit.
gitConfigHelpPullFfOnly: Only updates when the pull is a fast-forward. Otherwise it refuses and does not merge.
gitConfigHelpPullFfFalse: No always merges, even when a fast-forward is possible.
gitConfigHelpPushDefaultIntro: Which remote branch git push updates when you do not name one.
gitConfigHelpPushDefaultUnset: Default is simple on Git 2.0 and later.
gitConfigHelpPushSimple: Simple pushes the current branch only if its upstream has the same name. Harder to push the wrong branch.
gitConfigHelpPushCurrent: Current pushes the current branch to a remote branch of the same name, creating it if needed.
gitConfigHelpPushUpstream: Upstream pushes to the configured upstream even if the names differ.
gitConfigHelpColorUiIntro: Whether Git colors its command output.
gitConfigHelpColorAuto: Auto colors output in a terminal and uses plain text when piped.
gitConfigHelpColorAlways: Always colors even when piped or redirected. Can break scripts.
